name: India’s DPDP Act and Rules
question: What does Indian data-protection law require of my agent?
summary: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and its Rules (notified 13 November 2025) govern personal data processed in India. An agent that reads KYC documents or chats with customers is processing personal data, so it needs an itemised notice, specific consent or another lawful basis, collection limited to the purpose, reasonable security safeguards, contracts with processors such as model vendors, breach reporting and erasure when the purpose ends, including from vector stores and agent memory.
useCases: Any agent that sees customers’ personal data
Before sending personal data to a model vendor
When designing memory, logs and retention

items.detail: itemised, plain language, before or at collection
free, specific, informed; as easy to withdraw as to give
only the data the stated purpose needs
encryption, masking, access control, logs kept at least a year
inform the Board without delay; detailed report within 72 hours
delete when the purpose ends or consent is withdrawn

steps: Map every place personal data flows: prompts, retrieval, memory, logs, vendors
Write purpose-specific notices and consent, and record them
Mask or tokenise identifiers before they reach the model or logs
Build breach and erasure runbooks that reach every store
pitfalls: Deleting from the main database but not from embeddings, memory or caches
Sending raw Aadhaar or PAN details to an offshore model with no processor contract
Treating 13 May 2027 as far away: the data flows are being designed now
tools: Microsoft Presidio for PII detection and masking
Consent-management platforms, and registered consent managers from November 2026
Data-flow inventories in your GRC tool
Vault or cloud KMS for tokenisation keys
remember: Say why, ask specifically, take less, protect it, delete it, report breaches fast.
caption: Penalties are maximums set by the Act; dates as notified. Not legal advice.

steps.title: An itemised notice first
steps.text: Before collecting anything, tell the customer what data, for which purpose, and how to withdraw or complain, in plain English or a language they choose. The notice version is recorded with the consent.

steps.title: Consent per purpose
steps.text: KYC and marketing are separate purposes with separate records. The agent checks for active consent for this purpose before any processing.

steps.title: Take less: mask identifiers
steps.text: The model does not need a full Aadhaar number to check an address. Masking to the last four digits before the call keeps it out of prompts, vendor systems and logs.

steps.title: Bind the vendor
steps.text: A model vendor processing personal data for you is a data processor. A contract binds it to your purpose and safeguards; you remain responsible.

steps.title: Breach: fast, then in full
steps.text: Inform the Data Protection Board and affected people without delay, and give the Board a detailed report within 72 hours. A runbook makes that possible at 2 a.m.

steps.title: Erase every copy
steps.text: Erasure must reach the vector store, agent memory, caches and logs, not only the main database. Nivesh Credit’s first test reached 2 of 5 stores.

practice.scenario: Nivesh Credit, a fictional digital lender, mapped where personal data flowed through its onboarding agent after the DPDP Rules were notified. Full Aadhaar and PAN numbers were going into prompts to an offshore model with no processor contract, into the agent’s chat memory, and into debug logs kept indefinitely. An erasure test removed a customer from 2 of 5 stores. The team now masks identifiers before any model call, has a processor agreement with the vendor, keeps logs for a defined period, and sends erasure to all five stores.

numericDrill.question: A lender’s agent leaks customer data because identifiers were sent unmasked to a vendor, and the lender then fails to notify the Data Protection Board. Using the Act’s maximum penalties of ₹250 crore for failing to take reasonable security safeguards and ₹200 crore for failing to notify a breach, what is the combined maximum exposure, in ₹ crore?
numericDrill.answer: ₹250 crore + ₹200 crore = ₹450 crore. Actual penalties are set by the Board based on factors such as gravity, duration and mitigation, but the two failures are separate breaches of duty. Masking and a breach runbook remove both.

interview.question: What does the DPDP Act change for an AI agent that handles customer data?
interview.answer: Every place personal data flows becomes a compliance surface: prompts, retrieved context, agent memory, logs, caches and vendor calls. The agent needs a lawful basis and itemised notice for each purpose, collection limited to that purpose, safeguards such as masking and processor contracts, a breach process that reports without delay and in detail within 72 hours, and erasure that reaches every copy.

interview.question: When do the DPDP obligations apply?
interview.answer: The Rules were notified on 13 November 2025. The Data Protection Board provisions applied at once, consent managers follow after 12 months, and most substantive obligations, including notice, safeguards, breach reporting and erasure, apply from 13 May 2027. Systems designed now should meet them at launch.

mistakes.mistake: Erasing only from the primary database
mistakes.fix: Fan erasure out to vector stores, memory, caches and logs

mistakes.mistake: Raw identifiers in prompts and logs
mistakes.fix: Mask or tokenise before the model and the log see them

quiz.question: When were India’s DPDP Rules notified?
quiz.explanation: The Rules were notified on 13 November 2025.

quiz.question: From when do most substantive DPDP obligations, such as notice, safeguards and breach reporting, apply?
quiz.explanation: 18 months after notification: 13 May 2027.

quiz.question: After a personal-data breach, when is the detailed report to the Data Protection Board due?
quiz.explanation: Intimation without delay, then a detailed report within 72 hours.

quiz.question: What is the maximum penalty for failing to take reasonable security safeguards?
quiz.explanation: The Schedule caps it at ₹250 crore.

quiz.question: Which stores must an erasure request reach for an AI agent? Select all that apply.
options: The agent’s vector store of past chats
quiz.explanation: Every copy counts, including embeddings and memory.

quiz.question: A model vendor processes customer data on your instructions. What is it under the DPDP Act?
quiz.explanation: It processes on behalf of the fiduciary.

quiz.question: A customer consented to KYC processing. Can the same data be used for marketing without further consent?
options: No: consent is specific to a purpose
Only if anonymised by the model
quiz.explanation: Consent must be specific to each purpose.

quiz.question: Which is the most direct safeguard for Aadhaar numbers sent to an LLM?
options: Asking the model not to repeat them
quiz.explanation: Mask before the model and logs see them.

quiz.question: What is the maximum penalty for failing to notify the Board of a breach?
quiz.explanation: ₹200 crore under the Schedule.

quiz.question: Which belong in a DPDP-compliant notice? Select all that apply.
options: The personal data and the purpose
How to withdraw consent or complain
quiz.explanation: Itemised data and purpose, and how to exercise rights.

quiz.question: What must withdrawing consent be, compared with giving it?
quiz.explanation: Withdrawal must be as easy as giving consent.

quiz.question: When do consent managers begin operating under the Rules?
options: They are not in the Rules
quiz.explanation: From November 2026.

quiz.question: An agent keeps full chat transcripts forever “for future training”. What is the main DPDP issue?
quiz.explanation: Data should be erased when the purpose ends.

quiz.question: What must a fiduciary obtain before processing a child’s personal data?
quiz.explanation: Verifiable consent of a parent or guardian.

quiz.question: Which extra duty applies to a Significant Data Fiduciary?
options: Periodic data protection impact assessments and audits
quiz.explanation: SDFs have DPIAs, audits and algorithmic due diligence.

quiz.question: Some KYC records must be kept under other laws. What should happen on an erasure request?
options: Retain what law requires, restrict its use, and erase the rest
quiz.explanation: Erase what is not required and restrict what is.

quiz.question: Which tool detects and masks personal identifiers in text?
quiz.explanation: Presidio analyses and anonymises PII.

quiz.question: Who remains responsible if a vendor mishandles personal data it processed for you?
quiz.explanation: The fiduciary stays accountable.

quiz.question: Minimum retention floor for logs under the Rules, for specified purposes?
quiz.explanation: Logs and certain data are kept at least a year.

quiz.question: What is the best time to design DPDP controls into a new agent?
options: Now, while the data flows are being designed
quiz.explanation: Retrofitting is harder than designing in.
